title: Incident Cookbook: task-driven operator for support recipes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an "Incident Cookbook" service that lets support engineers author composable incident recipes (YAML or JSON) that execute as first-class tasks. Each recipe maps to a sequence of idempotent steps (queries, admin RPCs, shell adapters, playbooks) that can be executed, simulated (dry-run), audited, and rolled back. The goal is to replace ad-hoc runbook scripts with a safe, observable task runner surfaced in the Admin CLI and Console. Features: a lightweight recipe DSL, parameter validation, RBAC checks, KMS-backed secrets for step params, built-in retry/backoff, sandbox dry-run mode, automatic telemetry (per-step latency, success/failure, logs), and a step library for common ops (flush cache, route to fallback model, scale pool, revoke token).
acceptance_criteria: Users can create and register a recipe via Admin CLI and Console UI
Registered recipes run as tasks in the operator task queue with per-step tracing
Dry-run returns a deterministic plan without mutating downstream services
Audit log entries are emitted for each run with parameter redaction compliant with KMS policy
RBAC prevents non-privileged roles from invoking or editing recipes that contain privileged steps
End-to-end test that executes a sample 'cache-invalidate-and-verify' recipe in staging
Documentation and on-call quick-reference added to Confluence
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Chen: Created initial ticket after support rotation noted three incidents caused by ad-hoc shell scripts. Proposed a recipe-first model to reduce toil and improve auditability.

2026-03-03 - Rafael Ortiz: Spike completed to evaluate two approaches: extend existing operatorlet task runner vs. new lightweight 'cookbook' microservice. Chosen approach: extend operatorlet to reuse existing queue and tracing but add a recipe compiler module.
2026-03-04 - PM (Arjun Patel): Reviewed scope and requested explicit rollback step support for multi-step recipes; flagged need for canary execution mode for destructive steps.

2026-03-05 - Security (Leah Park): Requested KMS integration for secrets and that audit logs redact token-like parameters. Marked ticket for security design review before merging implementation changes.

2026-03-07 - Design (Olivia Ramos): Provided UX sketches for Console 'Run Recipe' flow and parameter modal. Suggested a confirmation checklist for destructive recipes and a preview pane that shows canonicalized plan.

2026-03-08 - Rafael Ortiz: Implemented recipe compiler prototype and a CLI subcommand 'rctl recipe run --dry-run'. Added unit tests for step idempotency detection. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operatorlet/pull/1862

2026-03-09 - QA (Dmitri Ivanov): Found a race when parallel runs access the same resource key; added requirement for resource locking primitives. Blocked acceptance until locking middleware implemented.
2026-03-10 - Rafael Ortiz: Added optimistic locking middleware and Sentry alert on lock conflicts; updated runbook docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Cookbook+Design
decisions: Extend operatorlet task runner instead of a separate service to reduce operational surface and reuse tracing/telemetry
Adopt a constrained recipe DSL (YAML) with a fixed set of step types to limit blast radius
Require KMS for secret parameters; store only encrypted blobs in recipe registry
Implement per-resource locking to serialize conflicting recipe runs
Expose both CLI and Console entrypoints; CLI prioritized for rapid on-call execution
